Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Mahama woos German investors with $10bn New Economy Programme Source : Myjoyonline.com 24 November 2026 6:49pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
President John Mahama has urged German businesses to increase investment in Ghana, announcing plans to commit US$10 billion to the country’s New Economy Programme over the next four years to accelerate industrialisation, create jobs and transform the economy.
Addressing the sixth German-African Business Summit in Accra, President Mahama said the programme, covering 2027 to 2030, would target key sectors including agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, tourism, the creative industry, digital innovation and mineral beneficiation.
He said Ghana was positioning itself as a competitive investment destination and a strategic gateway to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which provides access to a market of approximately 1.4 billion people.
The President said his government was seeking partnerships that extended beyond traditional development assistance to include trade, technology transfer, industrial cooperation, value addition and shared prosperity.
He cited improvements in Ghana’s economic performance as evidence of renewed investor confidence, noting that the economy grew by six per cent in 2025, while gross domestic product (GDP) had exceeded US$100 billion.
He also pointed to improvements in inflation and international reserves, as well as Ghana’s upgraded credit rating by Fitch, as indicators of progress in the country’s economic recovery.
President Mahama identified the government’s 24-hour economy initiative as another key part of its strategy to attract investment, maximise the use of productive assets, expand industrial operations, strengthen logistics and create employment.
He urged German businesses to see Africa as an interconnected investment and production destination rather than a collection of separate markets, with Ghana serving as an entry point.
As an example of successful bilateral investment cooperation, he cited the Nafshol apparel factory in Savelugu in the Northern Region, which received financing support from Germany’s KfW Development Bank.
According to him, the factory employs more than 2,000 young people, about 80 per cent of whom are women, providing jobs within their communities and reducing the need for young people to migrate southwards in search of employment.
The President also called for stronger business-to-business engagements, investment matchmaking and practical financing arrangements to turn discussions at the summit into concrete investments and commercial partnerships.
President of Germany, Dr Frank-Walter Steinmeier, also called for stronger economic relations between Germany and Africa, urging German businesses to take advantage of the continent’s growing investment opportunities.
He said trade between Germany and African countries increased by approximately 10 per cent in 2025 to reach a record high, although significant opportunities remained untapped.
Dr Steinmeier, who is undertaking one of his final official visits to Africa before the end of his presidency, said his numerous engagements across the continent had reinforced his belief that Africa and Europe needed each other.
He highlighted the entrepreneurship, creativity and dynamism of young Africans, particularly in technology and innovation, describing their skills and perspectives as valuable assets that could also benefit Europe.
He further stressed the need for stronger cooperation to address global challenges, including climate change, hunger, poverty and the rapid transformation being driven by artificial intelligence.
